title: Adult front-leg spike, force-probe, torque and observation bridge

scope.preparation: restrained fly pulling on the Azevedo et al. calibrated probe near 90 degrees, plus a model-derived unloaded tibia inertia prior
scope.claimBoundary: This artifact closes an experimental spike-to-probe observation path. It does not establish tendon moment arms, free-walking muscle geometry, extensor force calibration, or quantitative validity for the other five legs.

sources.title: A size principle for recruitment of Drosophila leg motor neurons

sources.note: Used only for disclosed one-spike class medians and uncertainty. These are publisher-figure-derived coordinates, not raw recordings or confidence intervals.

sources.title: NeuroMechFly v2 / FlyGym morphology
sources.note: Only two front-tibia morphology scalars are transcribed. No FlyGym controller, Python runtime, MuJoCo runtime or mesh is imported.

sources.title: Ultrasensitive fluorescent proteins for imaging neuronal activity
sources.license: PMC open manuscript terms; factual kinetics statements only

forceProbe.reference: Azevedo et al. Methods and Figure 1—figure supplement 2

motorUnits.reference: Azevedo et al. Results, Figure 4 and Figure 4 caption

gcamp6f.reference: Chen et al. 2013 Results and Figure 3
gcamp6f.note: This is a mouse cortical soma result, not a fit to the Mamiya fly axon preparation; it constrains only the order of the provisional observation filter.

morphologyPrior.derivation: Use the pinned FlyGym lf_tibia mass and the norm of its lf_tarsus1 child translation as tibia length; approximate the tibia as a uniform slender rod about one end, I = m L^2 / 3.
morphologyPrior.uncertainty: The source morphology is itself a model. The rod approximation omits shape, tarsal inertia, joint soft tissue and individual variation. It is reported separately from measured probe inertia.

forceCountCurve.reason: q = 0.6 makes F(2)/F(1) exactly 1.6 while producing the reported saturating response shape. F1 comes from the publisher-figure-derived median.

twitch.reason: The normalized exponential rise reaches half its 50 ms peak at 8.5 ms. Peak time follows the reported 50 ms optogenetic flash, while the fall constant remains a disclosed engineering value until raw traces are available.

torque.formula: joint torque = probe-equivalent muscle force * measured probe lever arm
torque.note: This is the joint torque implied by force measured at the probe. It deliberately avoids claiming an unknown tendon moment arm.

loadedJoint.derivation: Small-angle conversion at the measured lever arm: I = m r^2, K = k r^2, C = c r^2; add the separately labeled tibia rod inertia to I.

gcamp6fObservation.claimBoundary: A provisional low-pass and saturation observation layer. It is not fitted fly-axon GCaMP6f and cannot be used to manufacture driver overlap or correct the two remaining DSI failures.

heldOutMetrics.target: applied muscle force is recovered from spring + drag + probe inertia + tibia inertia within numerical tolerance
zero spikes produce zero active force and torque
reported ±1 SD lever arm uncertainty remains visible in torque bounds
a flexor burst decreases joint angle and drives flexion hook/club state without direct sensory injection
serialized bridge state continues bit-for-bit under the same inputs

knownLimitations: The Azevedo force curve is a restrained front-leg probe preparation, not a free-walking joint calibration.
Fast/intermediate one-spike magnitudes are publisher-figure-derived medians with digitization and between-cell uncertainty, not raw-data means.
The 50 ms peak and 25 ms relaxation choice are not a raw twitch fit.
The morphology prior is model-derived and the slender-rod calculation omits tarsi and soft tissue.
No tendon moment arm is claimed; the measured external probe lever arm supplies an experiment-specific torque observation.
BANC currently resolves some slow/fast flexor identities but not the Azevedo intermediate unit cleanly. Runtime population activity must not be relabeled as a known intermediate spike train.
Extensor forces remain relative because no equivalent absolute calibration is encoded.
The provisional GCaMP6f layer lacks raw Mamiya traces, preparation-specific baseline fluorescence, expression level, neuropil mixing and driver-overlap calibration.
